completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed test-zotero-generate-export.sh's unbounded runtime by rewriting synthesize_citekeys() as a single bulk jq pass and adding a 60s wall-clock bound with a proof-of-fire scenario; verified the whole suite (13/13 pass, ~12s), confirmed run-all.sh and the complete verify-deploy.sh gate set both now terminate deterministically (previously an indefinite hang), and closed the final verification phase COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS against 4 pre-existing, unrelated gate failures with full evidence.

memory_candidates.content: A per-item bash loop that re-invokes jq twice per element (once to index into the full array, once to re-serialize the full growing result) is O(N) subprocess spawns x O(N) JSON re-serialization -- quadratic overall. It looks fine at small N (the suite's other scenarios stayed under 350 items at 13-20s) and only reveals the cost at larger N, where it manifests as an apparent hang rather than a slow-but-finite result. Replacing the whole loop with a single `reduce .[] as $item` (or `reduce range(0; length)`) jq pass carrying an accumulator object as state collapses this to one process spawn and one O(N) pass. When auditing a bash+jq script for a mysterious hang, grep for a bash `for`/`while` loop whose body calls `jq` against a variable holding the full array (not a pre-sliced per-item chunk) -- that shape is the quadratic-cost signature.

When a foreground Bash tool call's inner `timeout N cmd` exceeds the harness's own ~590-600s foreground ceiling, the harness auto-backgrounds the call regardless of the inner timeout value -- the inner timeout does not prevent this. To run and reliably observe a command that may take longer than ~10 minutes without ending a turn on an unresolved wait: launch it explicitly with `nohup bash -c '...' > log 2>&1 & pid=$!`, save the pid, then poll with a bounded `kill -0 "$pid"` loop inside successive foreground Bash calls (each itself under the ceiling), reading the log for a final result once the pid dies. This is the same bounded-build-waiter shape, applied across multiple tool-call turns rather than one.
